sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Memphis?
sections.html:
Memphis is a large, river-based city, and a sale here is shaped by Shelby County offices more than by city hall alone. The county assessor values the property, the Board of Equalization hears value disputes, and the Register of Deeds records the deed. Knowing which office handles which step keeps a fast sale from stalling.

Census Bureau figures for mid-2025 show 609,647 people, about 3 percent fewer than the April 2020 base. Memphis spreads over roughly 297 square miles, and the median home value of $169,000 is a citywide figure. Price your expectations against your own street and the condition of your house.

sections.h2: How did the city's layout and economy come about?
sections.html:
Memphis sits on the Chickasaw Bluffs above the Mississippi River. John Overton, James Winchester and Andrew Jackson founded the modern city in 1819, and river trade and cotton built its early wealth. Today the largest employer is FedEx, whose global air hub operates at Memphis International Airport, and the Port of Memphis ranks as the fifth-busiest inland water port in the country.

Interstate 40 and Interstate 55 cross the Mississippi here, which is why logistics and warehousing dominate the job market. Census figures show the transportation and warehousing sector alone took in about $10.7 billion in receipts in 2022.

Memphis-Shelby County Schools serves the city, and the University of Memphis, LeMoyne-Owen College and Rhodes College are its main colleges. Overton Park in Midtown and the 4,500-acre Shelby Farms are the two large green spaces buyers mention most.

sections.h2: What do Memphis housing numbers say about my sale?
sections.html:
The next table draws on 2020 to 2024 estimates published by the Census Bureau. Because it describes the city as a whole, use it for context rather than as a price on your own house.

Owners live in fewer than half of Memphis homes, so rentals make up a large part of the housing stock. If tenants live in your house, give any buyer the lease terms and dates up front.

sections.h2: How does Memphis weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
The Memphis climate is hot and humid in summer. The city averages about 55 inches of rain a year and roughly 64 days above 90 degrees. Severe thunderstorms arrive mostly in spring, with hail, strong wind, flooding and the occasional tornado, and ice storms can bring tree limbs down onto roofs and power lines.

  • Roofs and gutters take the most wear from storms and heat, so check for missing shingles and sagging gutters.
  • Tree limbs over a roofline can come down in an ice storm.
  • Air conditioning age matters, since the summers are long and humid.

A buyer paying cash will usually price these items in and skip the repair negotiation. A buyer using a mortgage may ask for a roof or HVAC credit after the inspection.

sections.h2: How are Memphis property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Memphis sends its own city bill, apart from the one Shelby County issues. The City Council fixes the rate in June, and anything unpaid after August 31 becomes delinquent and grows by 1.5 percent each month. Values come from the Shelby County Assessor's roll as it stood on January 1.

Extra charges can ride along on the city bill: grass cutting, demolition and board-up, new sidewalk work and anti-neglect fees. Before listing, ask the City Treasury at 125 North Main Street for the current statement, since a closing agent will want every line cleared.

  • Owners 65 or older may qualify for the Tax Relief or Tax Freeze programs, both tied to income limits that the state resets yearly.
  • A Quarterly Payment Program lets homeowners 65 and up split the year into four equal parts, due August 31, November 30, February 28 and May 31.
  • Real estate taxes that remain unpaid after a full year go to delinquent tax attorneys the next February 1.

The county bill follows a different calendar. The Tennessee Comptroller's schedule makes county tax payable the first Monday of October, interest-free through February 28 and delinquent on March 1. Residential parcels are assessed at one quarter of appraised value.

sections.h2: Can I appeal my Memphis assessment, and when?
sections.html:
You could have, and the filing period has ended. The Shelby County Board of Equalization took challenges to 2025 values between May 1 and June 30, 2026. A value left unchallenged by then generally stands for the year, so phone the Board at (901) 222-7300 to learn when the next period opens.

Filing costs nothing. The Board's online eFile site only runs during appeal season, hearing notices go out two or more weeks ahead, and every exhibit has to be brought to the hearing itself. Results vary: a hearing can lower the value, raise it or leave it alone.

An easier first step is the Assessor's informal review. It is not a formal appeal, though the office says it clears up many disagreements. Helpful backup includes closed sales of comparable houses nearby, a recent private appraisal and dated photos of the property's condition. The Assessor's Action Center answers at 901-222-7001.

sections.h2: What happens at the Shelby County Register of Deeds when I sell?
sections.html:
Your deed is filed at the Register of Deeds office on Mullins Station Road (Building W-3, in the 38134 area of the city). By the office's own account, a recorded deed is typically back in the mail within a single business day, and a scanned image goes online. People who hold an e-file account can submit documents without a visit.

Recording triggers Tennessee's realty transfer tax, which the Department of Revenue prices at 37 cents for every $100 of the larger of sale price or fair value. Whoever receives the property, the grantee, owes that tax, and the grantee has to state the true consideration under oath on the instrument before the clerk will accept it.

Register's staff only record. They are barred from giving legal advice or helping with form wording, so lean on a closing attorney or title agent for the deed itself. If you need your earlier deed or a trust deed release, the office will find it and certify a copy.

sections.h2: Do short-term rental rules matter if I sell a Memphis house?
sections.html:
They can. Properties used as short-term rentals in Memphis must be registered through the Short-term Rental Registry kept by the Memphis and Shelby County Division of Planning and Development. A business in the city also needs both a City of Memphis and a Shelby County license, at $15 each. If you operate a rental out of the house you are selling, tell the buyer which registration it holds and gather the paperwork.

Ask the Division of Planning and Development for current fees and any pending changes before you list, since the City Council has been working on enforcement language for short-term rentals.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Memphis home sale?
faqs.a: The buyer owes it, as the person receiving title. The state charges 37 cents per $100 of the larger of price or value, and the Shelby County register takes payment at recording. Your contract may allocate it differently, so read that clause.

faqs.q: Is the Memphis assessment appeal window still open?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Equalization took appeals of 2025 assessments from May 1 through June 30, 2026. Call (901) 222-7300 for the next window, and use the Assessor's informal review at 901-222-7001 in the meantime.

faqs.q: What happens if I owe back city taxes on a Memphis house?
faqs.a: They accrue interest at 1.5 percent a month after August 31, and real estate taxes unpaid for a full year go to delinquent tax attorneys on the next February 1. Back taxes, plus any weed cutting or demolition charges on the bill, are normally settled out of your payout when the sale closes.

faqs.q: How quickly does Shelby County record a deed?
faqs.a: Within about one business day, according to the Register of Deeds, which mails the deed back and posts an image online. E-file account holders can send documents electronically.

faqs.q: Can a Memphis homeowner over 65 get property tax help?
faqs.a: Yes. The City offers a Tax Relief Program, a Tax Freeze Program and a Quarterly Payment Program for qualifying owners 65 or older, with the first two tied to state income limits. Contact the City Treasury at 901-522-1111 to apply.
